answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The quill multiplier is published, charged in island, and karst lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4230 identities would post 3431 proofs and burn roughly 66 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
